subject: Urgent: Reserved capacity shortfall + error surge impacting HorizonPay production
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@horizonpay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: HorizonPay Support <support@horizonpay.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production errors and latency spike — immediate assistance required

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx errors and end-to-end latency for our payments inference flows at ~08:50 PT. Traffic volume looks normal compared to our seasonality -- this appears to be a reserved-capacity throughput issue: queued requests are stacking and a subset are timing out with model errors (502/504). Attached are a small sample of request traces and the dashboard screenshot.

Impact:
- ~18% increase in p95 latency (from 240ms to ~1.7s)
- ~3% of requests are returning 5xx or timing out
- Several checkout flows are falling back to degraded UX; revenue impact measurable for current hour

We are on your Reserved plan (DEAL-HP-2027-003) with a pinned model and burst disabled. Can you please triage urgently and tell us whether you can:
1) enable burst capacity (hosted fallback) for the next 2 hours, or
2) temporarily route high-retry traffic to a warm hosted variant, or
3) apply any hotfix to reduce queueing on the dedicated pool.

We are ready for a quick bridge if needed — Ruth (CISO) is looped in on postmortem requirements.

Thanks,
Sandeep
VP Engineering, HorizonPay

Attachments: horizon_latency_logs_0728.zip, slo_dashboard_screenshot.png

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike — immediate assistance required

Sandeep — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're on it. Quick update and immediate asks: 

Immediate mitigation plan (next 90 minutes):
- [ACTION] I will request burst enablement for 2 hours to relieve queueing while we triage; Marissa please confirm business ok with temporary burst consumption and note any contractual constraints.
- [ACTION] Aditya and infra team will open an incident on the dedicated pool and check worker scaling + queue backpressure metrics.
- [ACTION] Evelyn will prep an exec summary and coordinate with our escalation channel so we can brief your CTO/CISO if needed.

Please confirm: are you comfortable with us routing up to 25% of traffic to a hosted variant while we stabilize? That is the quickest path to reduce p95. If not, we'll attempt in-pool worker changes first.

I'll schedule a 30-minute video bridge at 10:00 PT in case we need live troubleshooting.

— Priyom
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-28T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike — immediate assistance required

Adding a couple of account-specific details from our side:
- HorizonPay is on a 2x reserved GPU pool with a hard cap on burst per contract (DEAL-HP-2027-003). Legal ok'd one-time emergency burst but finance needs to track consumption for potential credits.
- Peak traffic this morning at 08:45 PT showed a sustained 3x spike for ~8 minutes which coincides with the error onset. Our reserved pool headroom was exhausted and autoscaler did not add additional workers due to an internal limit (we have that metric tracked).

Immediate asks for the infra team:
- Confirm whether autoscaler limits can be temporarily increased for this pool (Aditya).
- If burst is enabled, capture routing % so we can bill/credit accurately (Priyom).

Sandeep — happy to run the finance/contract thread in parallel; we can offer a one-time credit if the root cause is on our reserved capacity mis-provisioning. For now let's focus on stabilization.

— Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sandeep Rao <sandeep@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors and latency spike — immediate assistance required

Diagnostic summary (initial):
- Observed symptoms: p95 jump to ~1.7s, queue depth growth on reserved pool, elevated model-serve 502/504. KV cache miss rate increased ~4x on the affected model. No infra host failures detected.
- Probable vector: sudden request pattern with long input sequences and heavy KV miss churn. Dedicated pool hit headroom; autoscaler limit prevented additional workers from spawning.

Immediate technical actions taken (10:45–10:55 PT):
1) Enabled temporary burst routing rule for HorizonPay to allow up to 30% of inference traffic to be served by our hosted pool for 2 hours. Traffic steering applied and monitored.
2) Increased the reserved pool worker cap by +20% (temporary override) to give the dedicated pool more headroom.
3) Applied a short-lived model-variant with slightly lower max-seq (trading off longer outputs for execution reliability) to reduce per-request token work.

Current status (11:00 PT):
- p95 latency trending back toward baseline (now ~480ms) but still above SLO.
- 5xx rate reduced from ~3% to ~0.4%.
- Burst consumption currently at ~18% of traffic.

Next steps: incident postmortem, root cause analysis on input distribution, and a follow-up on autoscaler configuration to prevent hitting hard limits. I'll attach the lightweight runbook output after the bridge.

— Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: horizon_latency_logs_0728.zip

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@horizonpay.com>, Ruth Lin <ruth.lin@horizonpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-28T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Summary & exec asks — HorizonPay reserved-capacity incident (07/28)

Sandeep / Ruth — thank you for your patience this morning. Quick executive summary and asks so we can close the loop and agree the next steps.

What happened (brief):
- A short burst of long-sequence requests caused sustained KV cache churn; HorizonPay's reserved pool hit configured headroom limits and autoscaler did not spin additional workers because of a hard cap. That led to queueing and transient 5xx/timeouts.

What we did:
- Enabled temporary burst routing (~2 hours) and a hosted fallback variant (current redirect ~18%).
- Increased worker cap on the reserved pool temporarily (+20%).
- Deployed a short-lived lower-max-seq model variant to reduce per-request work.

Current status: service stabilized; p95 dropped from 1.7s to ~480ms; 5xx back to baseline.

Proposed remediation and asks:
1) We recommend updating the autoscaler hard cap for HorizonPay's reserved pool to allow faster scaling during short spikes (our recommended change will be in the postmortem). Please confirm if you want Redwood to implement that change on your behalf.
2) We will open a formal postmortem and share logs + mitigation timeline within 48 hours.
3) For this incident we propose a one-time credit to HorizonPay for excess burst usage if the postmortem shows mis-provisioning on our side. Marissa will follow up with finance for the credit estimate.

Decision request for your execs: please confirm whether:
A) We should permanently enable a soft-burst policy for HorizonPay (route up to X% to hosted during spikes), or
B) You prefer we rework autoscaler thresholds and keep burst off except for emergencies.

I'll set a short executive sync tomorrow at 10:00 PT to walk through the postmortem and proposed config changes.

— Priyom Das
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
